memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: ""I will take you as my own people, and I will be your God. Then you will know that I am the Lord your God, who brought you out from under the yoke of the Egyptians."" - Exodus 6:7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is the heart of it. God does not simply say, I will get you out of Egypt. He says, I will take you as my own people, and I will be your God.

That is the point of the whole rescue. Freedom was never the final goal. Relationship was.

We sometimes reduce salvation to escape — forgiveness of sins, rescue from judgement, a place in heaven. All of that is true and precious. But it is not the summit. The summit is that God takes us as His own and gives Himself to us.

This same covenant sentence echoes right through Scripture, and it reaches its final form in Revelation, where God dwells with His people and is their God (Rev 21:3).

Notice also the order: they will know Him as Lord after they experience His deliverance. Some things about God cannot be learned in a classroom. They are learned by being carried.

You are not merely forgiven. You are His.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I treat salvation mainly as escape, or as belonging to God?
2. What have I come to know about God only by being rescued by Him?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You did not only save me — You took me as Your own. Help me to live today as one who belongs to You. Amen.
